title: How Much More Trump Trouble Can Indonesia’s Prabowo Take?
gist: Derek Grossman argues Indonesian President Prabowo's efforts to align with Trump (Board of Peace and Gaza troops, a 19% tariff deal with China-related constraints, US military airspace access) have repeatedly backfired at home, worsened by the Iran war and new US trade probes. Still, Prabowo is too invested in Trump to reverse course and will make only marginal adjustments.

insights.claim: A March 2026 survey found 50.9 percent of Indonesians opposed membership in Trump's Board of Peace and 44.9 percent opposed deploying troops to Gaza, versus 33.8 percent in support.
insights.so_what: Domestic opinion constrains how far Jakarta can align with Washington on the Middle East.
insights.quote: a March 2026 survey found that 50.9 percent of respondents opposed Indonesia’s membership in the Board of Peace

insights.speaker: Derek Grossman

insights.claim: The Iran war led Prabowo to freeze Indonesia's Board of Peace engagement and suspend its planned Gaza troop deployment, conditioning any return on not disarming Hamas and on consent from Palestinian leaders and Egypt, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey.
insights.so_what: Indonesia's retreat undercuts the credibility of the US-led Gaza stabilization architecture.
insights.quote: In response, Prabowo froze Indonesia’s Board of Peace engagement and suspended its planned troop deployment to Gaza.
insights.locator: The Iran war has significantly worsened
insights.speaker: Derek Grossman

insights.claim: Prabowo denied ever committing money to the Board of Peace after reports Indonesia might contribute $1 billion, complicating the White House's portrayal of the body as an international success.
insights.so_what: Weakening partner commitments raise doubts about financing for Gaza reconstruction efforts.
insights.quote: Jakarta’s retreat complicates the White House’s portrayal of the Board of Peace as an international success story.
insights.locator: The Iran war has significantly worsened
insights.speaker: Derek Grossman

insights.claim: The Iran war has driven up energy costs, adding economic pressure on Indonesia's economy and consumers.
insights.so_what: Higher energy import costs pressure Indonesia's fiscal subsidies and consumer spending.
insights.quote: the war has driven up energy costs, creating additional concerns for Indonesia’s economy and consumers
insights.locator: The Iran war has significantly worsened
insights.speaker: Derek Grossman

insights.claim: Indonesia negotiated Trump's 32 percent April 2025 tariff down to 19 percent but in exchange agreed to align with US export controls and avoid trade deals that compromise 'essential U.S. interests', constraining its economic ties with China.
insights.so_what: US bilateral deals are being used to pull Southeast Asian economies away from China, affecting supply-chain and FDI flows.
insights.quote: Jakarta had to agree to restrictions in its economic relations with its other major partner, China.
insights.speaker: Derek Grossman

insights.claim: Indonesia signed its tariff deal one day before the US Supreme Court ruled Trump's tariffs illegal on Feb. 20, which the Jakarta Post called 'disastrous' timing.
insights.so_what: Countries that rushed to concede on tariffs may regret locked-in terms after legal reversals.
insights.quote: A commentary published by the Jakarta Post called the timing “disastrous,”
insights.locator: Prabowo would have rather moved on
insights.speaker: Derek Grossman

insights.claim: After the Supreme Court ruling, the Trump administration opened a Section 301 investigation into alleged Indonesian manufacturing overcapacity and a forced-labor probe, then imposed a 10 percent tariff on Indonesian goods in July despite Jakarta banning forced-labor imports.
insights.so_what: Section 301 is becoming the substitute tariff tool post-ruling, keeping trade-policy risk elevated for Southeast Asian exporters.
insights.quote: Washington nevertheless slapped Indonesian goods with a 10 percent tariff in July
insights.speaker: Derek Grossman

insights.claim: The ongoing US investigation into Indonesian excess manufacturing capacity remains an unresolved overhang on bilateral relations.
insights.so_what: Potential further tariffs on Indonesian manufactured exports remain a live risk.
insights.quote: Meanwhile, the U.S. investigation into excess capacity continues to hang over the relationship.
insights.speaker: Derek Grossman

insights.claim: Prabowo's reported approval of precleared US military access to Indonesian airspace triggered backlash, with the Defense Ministry denying a binding commitment and the Foreign Ministry warning it risked entangling Indonesia in a South China Sea conflict.
insights.so_what: Limits on US basing and access in Indonesia constrain US South China Sea contingency planning.
insights.quote: Indonesia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs warned that blanket U.S. access risked entangling the country in a South China Sea conflict
insights.speaker: Derek Grossman

insights.claim: Despite frictions, US-Indonesia cooperation is deepening through an expanding Super Garuda Shield exercise, growing critical minerals cooperation, and tens of billions of dollars in announced commercial deals.
insights.so_what: Critical minerals cooperation positions Indonesia as a non-China supply source for US industry.
insights.quote: U.S.-Indonesian critical minerals cooperation is also growing, and the two countries have announced tens of billions of dollars in new commercial deals.
insights.speaker: Derek Grossman

insights.claim: Because Prabowo has invested heavily in his personal relationship with Trump, the author expects only marginal adjustments rather than a reversal, such as appointing experienced diplomat Arrmanatha Nasir as foreign minister to scrutinize commitments before signing.
insights.so_what: Expect continuity in US-Indonesia alignment with more cautious deal-making, not a pivot to China.
insights.quote: he has invested heavily in both his personal relationship with Trump and the broader U.S.-Indonesia partnership, suggesting that he is unlikely to reverse course quickly
insights.locator: Yet some of the biggest advances
insights.speaker: Derek Grossman

insights.claim: Prabowo's skipping of this year's UN General Assembly is read by some Indonesian experts as a signal of growing frustration with Washington, though Jakarta officially cited domestic priorities.
insights.so_what: An early indicator of cooling in a key Southeast Asian partnership.
insights.locator: That Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto skipped
insights.speaker: Derek Grossman
